reason: The claim holds. VALUE: gated fusion of the fine-tuned and original secondary belongs to the I-126/I-335 family. I-126 is refuted because the edge-side gate is already in x138 (low_margin_consensus). I-335 is deferred with a prior <= 0: it reverts toward one model, and I-102 scored -0.002 on the LB. Detection-blend changes are 4/4 negative on the LB (I-156), and amanatar V6's max-blend bundle scored 0.901 (I-352, confounded). exp71 is a tiny change: rel L2 0.3-4.4% on 3 modules, and x138's per-frame mean/std alignment cancels the detect_head bias shift. The exp72 dummy moved nodes -0.16% and forks 75->80. A gate between two nearly identical maps therefore has ~0 expected effect, and there is no honest lab: both detectors were trained on all 199 videos, so disagreement measured in-sample means nothing. FEASIBILITY: a gate needs both secondaries encoded, ~+25% of the GPU phase (I-156 note). That takes the hidden run from 7.36-7.54 h toward ~9 h: still under 12 h, but it spends the safetail margin. More decisive is that R8 (27 Sep 12:00Z) has passed and this item has no user lift (only exp72 and an E10 port have one). So 'not re-proposed' is the only compliant action. One wording caveat: WiSE interpolation merges the weights into ONE network, so it costs no extra runtime. It is rejected on value only (it dilutes an already tiny delta back toward K2's secondary), not on the +25% runtime argument. The verdict does not change.
fix: Log as info under I-126/I-335. Keep the runtime argument (dual encode, +25%) for the gating variant only, and give WiSE alpha<1 its value-only reason (zero runtime cost, dilutes the change toward K2). No build, no slot, no GPU.
realistic_gain: 0 (expected public delta ~0.000; the gated or WiSE variant would most likely display 0.954 like K2/exp72, with a sign <= 0 prior from the reversion-to-one-model family).
